reasons: Tests the success path and the broken-recorder path.
The failure recording path is not tested in this file.

terms.meaning: automatic records about how the app runs, such as timings
a place where metric records are stored
extra labels attached to a record, such as a case ID

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports test tools and metric functions
sections.what: Brings in the test helpers and the metric pieces being checked.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps this test focused on the metrics module alone.

sections.name: lightweight internal metrics
sections.title: Metric recording checks
sections.what: Checks that a successful measured action is recorded with its operation name, a success outcome and its metadata, and that the result of the work comes back unchanged. Also checks that a recorder which throws does not stop the observe or measure helpers.
sections.why: Likely reason: tracking is a side job and must never change what the citizen receives.
sections.watch_out: Only the success path and the broken-recorder path are tested here.

summary: Tests that the internal timing helper records safe data without content and that a broken recorder never stops the main work.
purpose: Keeps the internal metrics trustworthy and confirms that a failure in telemetry is harmless to the citizen.
why: Likely reason: metrics should carry no personal content and must never stop an action the citizen takes.
how: Section one imports the metric functions and test tools. Section two checks that a measured operation is recorded with the right name, success outcome and metadata. It also checks that a recorder which throws does not stop the observe or measure helpers from returning normally.
inputs: No external inputs; it uses built-in test values.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The failure outcome path of the measure helper is not checked here, so a regression there would go unnoticed by this file.
debug: If a test fails, compare the recorded event with the expected shape in the test. Check the sink used in the test is the one the code writes to.
